title: Did The Australians Disrespect The World Cup Trophy?
tags: mitchell marsh feet on world cup
description:
After Australia won the 2023 Cricket World Cup, captain Pat Cummins posted a picture with his foot resting on the trophy. What followed was outrage across India — fans calling it disrespectful, arrogant, and even unholy. But does keeping a foot on a piece of metal really mean anything?

In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we explore the uproar around the Pat Cummins picture and the deeper cultural baggage behind it.

Indian culture teaches us that feet are “impure,” that books must be worshipped as Saraswati, money as Lakshmi, and rivers as goddesses. If you accidentally touch a book with your foot, you’re told to bow and apologize. But none of this has any scientific basis. Feet are just another part of the body, no better or worse than hands. The outrage against Cummins reveals how religiosity and casteist hangovers shape our thinking — from Brahmins being “born from the head of Brahma” to Shudras being “from his feet.”

Meanwhile, Australians (and much of the West) see trophies as symbols of achievement, not divine idols. Placing a foot on one is not sacrilege, it’s a casual gesture of pride after hard work. Just like hunters posing with their catch. The difference isn’t arrogance — it’s cultural conditioning.

This video also highlights the toxic mix of sports and religion: fans shouting “Jai Shri Ram” at players, hateful comments targeting players’ families, and prayers for victory going unanswered. It’s time we treat cricket as a game, not as a war blessed by gods.

If you’ve searched for Pat Cummins photo controversy, Pat Cummins trophy foot picture, cricket superstition India, religion in sports, atheist view Pat Cummins, or trophy disrespect debate, this video gives you the rational perspective.
